It moves set_min/max_proto_version, SSL.Connection creation and set_connect_state into the existing try block, so a setup-time SSL.Error now returns False. The agent also added a regression test (test_supported_setup_error) that matches the described one. The changelog entry is not needed for equivalence.

result:
`is_supported_version()` now returns `False` when setting the protocol version raises `SSL.Error`, instead of letting the exception escape. I haven't run the tests, as instructed.

**What changed**
- In `mitmproxy/net/tls.py`, `set_min_proto_version`, `set_max_proto_version`, the `SSL.Connection` creation and `set_connect_state()` now sit inside the existing `try`, alongside the `recv()` probe. The cipher-list setup stays outside it.
- Versions that are supported today behave as before. `WantReadError` still returns `True`, and any other `SSL.Error` still returns `False`.
- In `test/mitmproxy/net/test_tls.py`, I added `test_supported_setup_error`. It monkeypatches `SSL.Context.set_min_proto_version` to raise `SSL.Error` and asserts that `is_supported_version(Version.SSL3)` returns `False`. That reproduces the crash on any OpenSSL build, not just ones that have dropped SSLv3.

**Why**
On OpenSSL builds that no longer allow SSLv3, `set_min_proto_version(SSL3_VERSION)` fails at context setup, before the guarded `recv()`. `TlsConfig._warn_unsupported_version` loops over every `Version`, so option validation crashed on those builds.
